lead.title: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics and the MINIGRAPH consortium (EIC) validate a graphene implant for deep brain stimulation, with electrode stability projected beyond 10 years
lead.deck: The European project, coordinated by ICN2 (Catalonia) with ETH Zurich, Fraunhofer, imec and LUMC, validated an integrated prototype of graphene probes that decode activity across hundreds of neural sites, plus a minimally invasive delivery route using magnetic navigation designed with Nanoflex Robotics and tested in a large animal model. First target: Parkinson's disease; no patient has been implanted in this project yet, which remains preclinical.

milestone.title: Sonorous wins FDA IDE for the B-SILENT 2 pivotal trial of its BosSTENT for pulsatile tinnitus
milestone.summary: BosSTENT is a self-expanding stent for the cerebral venous sinuses; it received FDA Breakthrough Device designation in February 2026 and B-SILENT 2 enrolment is expected in Q4 2026. The separate B-SILENT study is already enrolling at six sites in France and Canada.
milestone.why: A niche indication with no dedicated treatment moves into a pivotal phase: the signal of a company approaching a marketing application, with part of the clinical data generated in Europe.

deal.thesis: Breega leads this seed (with Enzo, Heartfelt, Together Ventures and Bynd) for an AI platform that turns a simple trial brief into a full protocol, submission package and operational plans aligned with current regulation. The bet: fewer trial delays, hence shorter time-to-market for devices and drugs.

brefsIntl.title: Abbott gets FDA approval for updates to its CardioMEMS heart failure monitoring sensor
brefsIntl.summary: Patients will see their pulmonary artery pressure on a smartphone and receive medication updates; clinicians will adjust drugs through a dynamic treatment plan, available later in 2026. A benchmark for every European implantable-monitoring player.

brefsIntl.title: OXOS Medical wins a BARDA contract worth up to $24.4M for its ultra-portable OXOS X3 x-ray system
brefsIntl.summary: Cost-share contract: OXOS matches the contribution, for a potential total value of $48.8M. It shows US public funders' appetite for imaging deployable outside the hospital.

brefsIntl.title: GE HealthCare to acquire Sofie Biosciences for $945M to enter radiopharmaceutical manufacturing and distribution
brefsIntl.summary: A valuation comparable: device majors are paying up for tracer production infrastructure as theranostics grows.

word.fr: Magnetic steering of devices from outside the body
word.definition: Magnets steer the tip of a catheter or probe through vessels or the brain from outside the body, so the physician does not push the tool by hand.

parts.label: Magnetic field unit
parts.role: the pilot: generates the field that orients the tool

parts.label: Magnetised tool
parts.role: the vehicle: a catheter, guidewire or probe whose tip responds to the field

parts.label: Imaging and software
parts.role: the GPS: x-ray and real-time tracking to guide the path

how.t: The surgeon defines the trajectory from the patient's imaging.
The magnetic unit orients the tool tip through small adjustments of the field.
Imaging confirms the position; the operator can drive from a console, even remotely.

word.why: VC angle: it opens up tele-intervention (remote thrombectomy, minimally invasive brain access) and makes surgical expertise scalable; the barrier is regulatory and capital-intensive, but early installers build a clinical dataset that is hard to catch up with.

startups.name: Nanoflex Robotics
startups.use: ETH Zurich spin-off: its Remote Intervention System magnetically guides endovascular devices, targeting stroke thrombectomy (Series A of over $12M led by Ascend Capital Partners).

startups.name: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics
startups.use: Uses a magnetic-navigation delivery route, designed with Nanoflex and ETH Zurich, to place its graphene probes in the MINIGRAPH project (Parkinson's).

startups.name: Stereotaxis
startups.use: Listed incumbent (NYSE: STXS): its Genesis robotic magnetic navigation system for electrophysiology keeps landing in new European hospitals, including the University of Szeged in Hungary in July 2026.
